subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After a deferred maintenance timeout releases the session lane, should OpenClaw keep later same-session maintenance coalesced until the original plugin call settles, or introduce a cancellable context-engine contract that makes immediate replacement safe?
rationale: The branch deliberately releases the lane for liveness, while current main's lifecycle guarantees one active deferred maintenance owner per session. Choosing whether timeout changes that guarantee is a persistent plugin/runtime contract decision, not a mechanical review preference.

options.title: Keep coalescing until settlement
options.body: Release the foreground lane at timeout but retain a fenced per-session run record so later maintenance requests only coalesce until the original call settles.

options.title: Design explicit cancellation
options.body: Add and document a context-engine cancellation contract, then start a replacement only after cancellation has been acknowledged or otherwise made safe.

options.title: Do not land this mode
options.body: Keep the existing unbounded deferred-maintenance behavior until one of the above contracts is implemented and proven.

recommendation.title: Keep coalescing until settlement
recommendation.body: Release the foreground lane at timeout but retain a fenced per-session run record so later maintenance requests only coalesce until the original call settles.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent command-lane timeout and runtime lifecycle history makes this the strongest available owner signal for the contract choice.
